hypothesis: Theorems TA-1 and TA-2 predict, on the 4-bit Boolean world with three context subsets U_1={x_0=0}, U_2={x_1=0}, U_3={x_2=0} and target label space T=Z/4, that (i) the good chart family with transitions T_12=+1, T_23=+1, T_13=+2 satisfies the cocycle on the single triple (1,2,3) and glues to a global theory M(x) = (2*x_2+x_3) mod 4; (ii) the bad chart family with transitions T_12=+1, T_23=+1, T_13=+3 violates the cocycle (discrepancy = shift-by-3 on Z/4, rank 4) and does not glue; and (iii) the bad-family cocycle failure has the missing-latent signature (rank>=1 with all three T_ij non-identity), distinct from the phase-transition/boundary signature (rank>=1 with exactly one T_ij non-identity).

controls.description: Every T_ij is constructed as a permutation of T (bijection on the 4-element target label space); permutation validity is enforced by construction and re-checked by tests.

The chart maps M_i are identical between the good and bad families; only the transitions T_ij differ, so the gluing verdict is a pure function of the transition data and cannot be smuggled through the chart definitions.

A third phase_boundary_reference family (T_12=+1, T_23=id, T_13=id) is evaluated alongside the good and bad families as an explicit control that Theorem TA-2's rank/support taxonomy distinguishes the phase-transition case from the missing-latent case on identical machinery.

The cocycle discrepancy identity check and the pivot-through-chart-1 gluing attempt are independent computations that must agree on both families -- an internal cross-check of Theorem TA-1's equivalence.

gates.criterion: For the good chart family, the cocycle T_jk ∘ T_ij = T_ik holds on every triple (i,j,k) with pairwise overlap (equivalently, cocycle_discrepancy is the identity permutation on T).
For the bad chart family, at least one triple (i,j,k) has non-zero cocycle discrepancy (rank >= 1 on T).

The pivot-through-chart-1 gluing attempt is consistent (returns a single-valued global M) for the good family and inconsistent (assigns at least one world multiple candidate values on the overlaps) for the bad family.

The bad family is classified as 'missing_latent' by Theorem TA-2's rank/support rule (cocycle fails AND every pairwise T_ij is non-identity), while the phase_boundary_reference family is classified as 'phase_transition' (cocycle fails AND exactly one pairwise T_ij is non-identity), and the good family is classified as 'glue'.
